analysis:
Examined the head tail of ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift (lines 1146-1543) and the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift patch with its base text. Only a partial patch excerpt of the handler is visible, so the new decodeInboundChatRequest and the WorkFIFOGate plumbing could not be assessed in full.

Serve.swift changes: (1) the work consumer now calls awaitReleasedAdmissions() before every event that does not overtake released admissions. (2) .inferenceRequest is wrapped in admitInWorkFIFO, which passes a WorkFIFOGate into handleInferenceRequest. (3) .cancel is deferred via deferCancelForReleasedAdmission. (4) The consumer awaits all admissions at stream end. These are availability and ordering changes in the consumer for TB-002 and T-010.

The ordering helper file ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift is not supplied, so these points are unverified:
- Whether .disconnected, .drainAck and .connected correctly wait for or cancel released admissions. In the visible code .disconnected is not an overtaking event unless overtakesReleasedAdmissions says so, and the cancelAllInflight semantic depends on that helper.
- Whether a deferred cancel is eventually applied. A lost cancel would leave GPU and memory in use (T-010).
- Whether a stuck model load could block cancel, attestation challenge or heartbeat handling. The App Attest and trust controls run on the separate eventTask reader (lines 395-418), which is unchanged, so connection-control and grant handling stay unblocked.

The visible handler tail shows no security-relevant change. It shows no plaintext SSE on encryption failure (T-008), the response hash domain is unchanged, billing floors are unchanged, and the cache usage fields come from the signal. The 'withheld reasoning' references (firstWithheldReasoningAt, generatedReasoningText, reasoningLogprobs) are new or changed behavior. Their definitions are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm that withheld reasoning is excluded from the response hash and attestation signature. The code comment says it is, and fullResponseText is built from the same emitted frames, which is consistent. Cache outcome fields remain gated on remoteCache.scope (T-041 unchanged).

No concrete regression is established. A deeper review should cover ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift and the head portion of the handler (decodeInboundChatRequest, the template controls extraction, and the gate release paths).
